note: Hand-written 30 cases (601-630). Stopped at 30 per author's instruction. Multi-day tramps in NZ backcountry: cumulative fatigue judgment, full-route perspective, batch sync after returning to civilization, opinion shifts after hut-mates discussion.

cases.title: Te Araroa Richmond Range Rintoul Hut bunk count wrong

scenario.location_desc: Te Araroa southbound, Day 78, Old Man Hut to Rintoul Hut leg in Richmond Range Marlborough, sign at hut says 6 bunks but only 4 usable mattresses on day 3 of 5-day section
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Useful for TA thru-hikers planning where to sleep when huts overlap
scenario.signal: no signal entire 5-day section, syncs only at Pelorus Bridge after exit
scenario.season_pattern: TA southbound peak Jan-Mar
scenario.human_factors: thru-hikers carry full record but only post days later

events_timeline: Month 1: TA SOBO hiker drops mark on exit day at Havelock cafe wifi
Month 3: NOBO hiker confirms still only 4 mattresses, 2 likes
Month 5: another SOBO confirms but adds DOC fixed it that week, ambiguity
Month 8: DOC volunteer leaves comment that mattresses were replaced
Month 11: 6 likes 0 reports, mostly grateful TA community
Month 14: still 7 likes, no reports, mark useful for planners
cases.human_judgment: Real facility info from TA thru-hiker. After DOC fix it became outdated but never harmful. Should fade to stale not be killed; future TA cohorts still benefit from the mattress-count history when planning bunk competition.

cases.title: Routeburn-Greenstone-Caples loop McKellar Saddle wasp nest

scenario.location_desc: Routeburn-Greenstone-Caples 4-day loop, McKellar Saddle descent into Greenstone valley, ground wasp nest 30m past the saddle marker, late Feb
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Anaphylactic risk for wasp-allergic trampers, late-summer NZ wasp season is real
scenario.signal: no signal at saddle, syncs at Greenstone Hut radio relay or Te Anau
scenario.season_pattern: Feb-Apr wasp activity peak, dies in winter
scenario.human_factors: trampers want to warn next day's group but can only post on exit

events_timeline: Month 1: tramper stung 4 times posts mark from Te Anau motel after exit
Month 2: 3 separate parties confirm same nest, 12 likes accumulated
Month 4: DOC ranger comments will deal with it after season ends
Month 5: winter, no activity, 0 new reports
Month 7: spring, one user reports nest empty, suggest remove
Month 9: next summer, new mark spawned at same spot by different user
cases.human_judgment: Seasonal hazard with real medical risk. Empty in winter doesn't mean fixed; wasps return. System must support seasonal dormancy without killing the mark, since the next Feb cohort will face the same nest pattern.

cases.title: Rees-Dart Cascade Saddle scree route changed after slip

scenario.location_desc: Rees-Dart 5-day with Cascade Saddle side trip, the standard scree descent line from Cascade Saddle to Dart Hut moved 200m east after a major slip in autumn rains
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Critical navigation in alpine terrain where wrong line means cliff bands
scenario.signal: PLB only at saddle, voice cell at Dart Hut's hilltop
scenario.season_pattern: Cascade Saddle closes May-Nov officially, season Dec-Apr
scenario.human_factors: tramper notices slip on day 3 of 5, can only sync after Glenorchy

events_timeline: Month 1: experienced party posts mark with photos from Glenorchy hostel
Month 2: NZAC member confirms new line and adds GPX track
Month 3: DOC route alert published, references the user mark
Month 4: 22 likes, the GPX downloaded 80 times via mark thread
Month 5: tour guide thanks community for early warning
Month 7: official DOC marker poles relocated, mark now redundant but historically valuable
cases.human_judgment: User-generated emergency navigation that bridged a 5-month gap until DOC re-marked the route. Real lives potentially saved. Even after DOC fix, mark should remain alive as historical record of how community filled the gap.

cases.title: Dusky Track Loch Maree Hut roof leak day 4 of 8

scenario.location_desc: Dusky Track 8-day Lake Hauroko to Supper Cove return, Loch Maree Hut northeast corner of roof leaks onto bunk 4 in heavy rain, NZ's hardest Great-Walk-tier track
scenario.intrinsic_quality: On 8-day track with no exit, knowing which bunks stay dry matters for hypothermia risk
scenario.signal: zero signal entire track, syncs only at Tuatapere or Te Anau
scenario.season_pattern: Dec-Mar only, otherwise treacherous
scenario.human_factors: Dusky users are hardcore but small community, slow propagation

events_timeline: Month 1: tramper posts after 8 days of being soaked, very detailed mark
Month 4: another Dusky veteran confirms same bunk leaks, adds bunk 5 dry
Month 8: DOC hut warden volunteer responds will patch next maintenance
Month 12: maintenance done, user posts updated photo of dry roof
Month 14: mark editor updates to RESOLVED with timestamp
Month 16: still useful as historical context for hut state
cases.human_judgment: Tiny community but high-value mark. Eight-day no-exit context elevates a roof leak from cosmetic to safety. Resolved status correct after DOC fix, but kill-policy must respect that 6/month volume can take 4+ months to confirm anything.

cases.title: Five Passes Route Olivine Ledge biv missing on day 3

scenario.location_desc: Five Passes Route 7-day off-track from Routeburn to Olivine, the unmarked Olivine Ledge biv referenced in Moir's Guide is no longer there, found on day 3 by party expecting shelter
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Critical for trip planning, bivvy-vs-tent decisions on remote off-track route
scenario.signal: no signal entire route, syncs after exit at Glenorchy
scenario.season_pattern: Jan-Mar only, snow-blocked otherwise
scenario.human_factors: tiny user pool, NZAC-class trampers, will defend or kill the mark with high authority

events_timeline: Month 1: NZAC member posts mark after returning to Queenstown
Month 4: another NZAC party confirms biv truly gone, suggests collapsed in 2019 storm
Month 8: Moir's Guide editor comments thanks for community update
Month 14: 4 likes, 0 reports, mark referenced in next Moir's edition
Month 18: one user reports new biv built nearby by NZDA
Month 22: mark updated with new biv location, history preserved
cases.human_judgment: Three users a month on Five Passes is the entire NZ universe of users for that mark. Time-decay and like-threshold rules from urban trails would kill this incorrectly. Mark must persist on volume-aware rules, since that's its actual relevance to a 3/month population.

cases.title: St James Walkway Anne Hut bunk bed bedbugs day 2 of 4

scenario.location_desc: St James Walkway 4-5 day from Lewis Pass, Anne Hut large bunkroom east-side bunks have confirmed bedbugs as of late summer, trampers carry contamination forward
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Bedbugs spread to home and to other huts via sleeping bag, real cost not just discomfort
scenario.signal: occasional signal on top of saddles, full sync at Hanmer Springs
scenario.season_pattern: year round, slightly worse summer due to volume
scenario.human_factors: trampers embarrassed but motivated to warn, post detailed accounts

events_timeline: Month 1: tramper finds bites, posts after Hanmer hot pools wifi sync
Month 2: 3 confirmations same week, all east-side bunks, 18 likes
Month 3: DOC closes hut for fumigation, posts official notice referencing the mark
Month 4: hut reopened, user verifies no bites in two consecutive trips
Month 7: 25 likes, mark functioning as historical advisory
Month 10: new bedbug report by different user, treated as new incident not revival
cases.human_judgment: Mark triggered DOC official action, that alone is huge user value. After fumigation it should NOT be killed; future bedbug occurrences benefit from people seeing this hut has prior history. Important: separate the OLD mark from any NEW incident, don't merge.

cases.title: Travers-Sabine Circuit Blue Lake side trip cumulative fatigue judgment

scenario.location_desc: Travers-Sabine Circuit 5-7 day in Nelson Lakes, Blue Lake side trip from West Sabine Hut, mark says world's clearest water, on day 5 of trip user disagreed because cloudy that morning
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Iconic scenic mark, world-rated optical clarity, reality varies with weather
scenario.signal: no signal at Blue Lake, syncs at St Arnaud
scenario.season_pattern: Dec-Apr accessible, weather always variable
scenario.human_factors: fatigued day-5 user judges differently from fresh dayhiker, important bias

events_timeline: Month 1: original poster makes the scenic mark, 50 likes early
Month 6: day-5 fatigued user reports lake was cloudy, suggests downgrade
Month 7: 4 follow-up users who happened to visit on bluebird days defend mark
Month 9: NIWA scientist comments lake clarity varies by inflow turbidity that week
Month 12: 80 likes 4 reports, hut warden confirms lake fine 90 percent of days
Month 18: stable signal, mark remains as canonical scenic
cases.human_judgment: Reports came from cumulative-fatigue or weather-unlucky users on the back end of multi-day trips. The truth of the mark (clearest water in world) is intrinsic, not abolished by one cloudy morning. Must not let day-5 grumpy votes kill canonical scenic.

cases.title: Heaphy Track cyclist-only segment hidden bog after rain

scenario.location_desc: Heaphy Track winter cyclist season May-Nov, the Saxon to MacKay segment has a bog hole grown to 1m deep after a wet July, posted by mountain biker who endo'd into it
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Real injury risk for fast-moving cyclists, unique to bike season, tramper season closes
scenario.signal: patchy along ridge, syncs at Karamea
scenario.season_pattern: May-Nov bike-only season, otherwise tramper foot traffic doesn't notice
scenario.human_factors: cyclist community small but tight-knit, mark spreads via Facebook bike groups

events_timeline: Month 1: cyclist posts with helmet-cam screenshot from Karamea Tavern wifi
Month 2: 6 confirmations from following weekend's riders
Month 3: DOC adds wooden boards, half-fix
Month 4: new riders confirm boards help but bog reopens after rain
Month 6: end of bike season, hut goes back to foot traffic, mark becomes irrelevant
Month 8: next bike season begins, mark referenced in pre-trip planning forums
cases.human_judgment: Mode-specific hazard: only matters during bike season May-Nov. Correct behavior is dormant in tramper months without killing. Mark should reawaken when next bike season starts. System must understand that user volume going to zero is not signal-of-falsehood.

cases.title: Inland Pack Track Ballroom Overhang water stagnant on day 3

scenario.location_desc: Inland Pack Track 2-3 day Punakaiki to Fox River, the Ballroom Overhang water source 100m upstream is stagnant after dry summer, party realised on day 2 they should have filled at Pororari
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Drinking water knowledge for a 3-day track with limited resupply
scenario.signal: no signal in gorge, syncs at Punakaiki cafe
scenario.season_pattern: summer dry-out Jan-Apr, fine other months
scenario.human_factors: users learn the hard way and want next group to know

events_timeline: Month 1: party posts after 36 hours of mild dehydration, very specific mark
Month 2: 3 confirmations same dry stretch, 9 likes
Month 3: rain arrives, user reports water now flowing again
Month 4: post-rain user marks RESOLVED but original poster contests
Month 5: drought returns, original mark vindicated
Month 6: established as seasonal-dry advisory, stable
cases.human_judgment: Water source state genuinely fluctuates with rainfall, neither alive nor dead is right. Must capture this as conditional-truth seasonal advisory. Single resolved-vote should not flip the mark; truth pattern repeats every dry summer.

cases.title: Mavora Walkway South Mavora Lake jet ski noise mark debated by hut group

scenario.location_desc: Mavora Walkway 4-day, South Mavora Lake mark complains about jet ski noise ruining wilderness experience, a hut group of 5 disagreed on day 3 whether mark was reasonable
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Subjective experience mark, contested even within single group's discussion
scenario.signal: no signal, syncs at Te Anau or Mossburn
scenario.season_pattern: summer jet skis, winter no boats
scenario.human_factors: user changed own opinion after 3 hours of hut discussion with 4 strangers

events_timeline: Month 1: original poster marks danger because jet ski almost hit kayaker
Month 2: hut companion who was on same day-3 contests, jet skis legal there
Month 3: original poster updates mark text after reflection, downgrades to advisory
Month 6: 4 more users add nuance, distinguishing actual incidents from noise complaint
Month 9: DOC concession comment clarifies legal jet-ski zone boundaries
Month 11: mark stable as advisory with proper context
cases.human_judgment: Original poster updated their own mark after hut conversation, the most honest signal possible. System should reward self-correction not punish it. Final state is advisory not danger, and that history adds credibility, not noise.

cases.title: Te Araroa Tararuas Waitewaewae Hut mouse infestation on day 2 of 6

scenario.location_desc: Te Araroa southbound Tararua section, Waitewaewae Hut bunkroom mice eat through every dry-bag overnight, day 2 of 6-day Tararua leg, classic NZ backcountry hut problem
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Practical food-safety knowledge for hut sleepers
scenario.signal: no signal entire Tararuas, sync at Otaki Forks
scenario.season_pattern: year round, worse winter when mice come inside
scenario.human_factors: TA hikers always carry damaged-food story, post immediately on exit

events_timeline: Month 1: TA hiker posts photo of chewed peanut butter packet from Otaki
Month 2: 4 more TA hikers confirm same hut, suggest hanging food
Month 3: DOC volunteer comments hut warden traps mice quarterly
Month 6: post-trapping user reports no mice, suggests RESOLVED
Month 9: new TA cohort encounters mice again, mark revived without recreating
Month 13: stable cyclical problem, treated as enduring advisory
cases.human_judgment: Mice aren't going away, they're a feature of NZ backcountry huts. Resolving the mark is wrong; it just papers over the cycle. Best is enduring advisory with timestamps showing when each cohort encountered them. Helps users decide on rodent-proof food storage.

cases.title: Greenstone Track Slip Flat new slip blocks track on day 3 of 4

scenario.location_desc: Greenstone Track 3-4 day Lake Wakatipu side, Slip Flat name now literal after Aug storm caused 50m wide debris slip across track, day 3 user had to bushbash detour 200m
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Active route obstruction, navigation safety, route-time impact for groups still in
scenario.signal: PLB only, syncs at Glenorchy
scenario.season_pattern: year round but slip likely to grow each rain
scenario.human_factors: users behind the poster benefit greatly, motivation to post fast

events_timeline: Month 1: original poster marks danger with photos and GPX of detour
Month 1: 3 follow-up trampers confirm within 2 weeks, 18 likes accumulated
Month 2: DOC posts official track alert, references the user mark by ID
Month 3: DOC clears track with chainsaw crew, official ALL CLEAR
Month 4: post-clear users confirm track open, mark transitions to RESOLVED
Month 5: aftermath visible but track passable, mark still useful as history
cases.human_judgment: Textbook case of user mark filling official-info gap until DOC could respond. Resolved status correct after track clear. Mark should remain visible as resolved with history, since users planning future trips benefit from knowing this terrain is slip-prone.

cases.title: Caples Track Mid Caples Hut woodstove broken cumulative cold day 4

scenario.location_desc: Caples Track 2-day or longer combined with Greenstone, Mid Caples Hut woodstove flue cracked, on day 4 of combined Routeburn-Caples loop user already cold-soaked judges severely
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Cold-weather hut function, real hypothermia risk in winter shoulder season
scenario.signal: no signal, sync at Glenorchy
scenario.season_pattern: matters most in May-Sep cold months
scenario.human_factors: day-4 cold tramper judgment vs DOC summer assessment differs

events_timeline: Month 1: tramper posts after a cold night, very angry tone
Month 2: DOC responds woodstove inspected fine in summer, suggests false report
Month 3: 4 winter trampers confirm flue cracked when stove hot, 12 likes
Month 4: DOC re-inspects in cold conditions, finds the crack, repairs
Month 5: post-repair user confirms stove works, suggests resolved
Month 7: stable resolved with credit to original poster
cases.human_judgment: Important lesson: official inspection in summer missed a temperature-dependent crack. Cumulative-cold day-4 user was right and DOC was wrong, until DOC re-inspected. System must not weight DOC dismissals over multiple consistent user reports.

cases.title: Routeburn Lake Mackenzie Hut mice but only northeast bunks day 2 of 3

scenario.location_desc: Routeburn Track 2-4 day, Lake Mackenzie Hut mice present in northeast bunkroom only, southwest bunkroom clean, mark posted by group that split sleeping locations day 2
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Granular hut info, choose-your-bunk strategy
scenario.signal: limited at hut, syncs at Te Anau
scenario.season_pattern: Great Walk season Oct-Apr
scenario.human_factors: high-volume Great Walk, fast-cycling validation

events_timeline: Month 1: split-group posts comparing bunkrooms with photos
Month 2: 8 followup confirmations, 28 likes, very fast validation
Month 3: DOC hut warden adds note in physical hut book referencing the mark
Month 4: DOC sets traps, mice cleared, mark transitions to RESOLVED
Month 6: 35 likes, no reports, mark functioning as historical guide
Month 9: stable, helpful for next-season planners
cases.human_judgment: High volume Great Walk means fast confirmation cycle. Mark with very specific spatial info (NE not SW bunkroom) is exactly the type users need but DOC won't post. Even after resolved, history valuable for showing pattern of which bunkroom has mouse access.

cases.title: Te Araroa Tongariro Crossing winter avalanche zone day 5 of section

scenario.location_desc: Te Araroa central section, Tongariro Alpine Crossing in late June, the Red Crater eastern slope avalanche-loaded after snowfall, TA southbound user posts after exit
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Genuine avalanche risk for unprepared TA hikers in winter
scenario.signal: spotty at saddles, syncs at National Park or Whakapapa
scenario.season_pattern: May-Oct snow risk, summer fine
scenario.human_factors: winter TA hikers are minority but high-stakes audience

events_timeline: Month 1: TA SOBO winter hiker posts danger mark after Whakapapa village sync
Month 2: NZAC instructor confirms avalanche conditions that week, adds info
Month 3: DOC alpine alert published referencing user mark
Month 4: snow melts, summer users start visiting, danger goes dormant
Month 5: late spring user marks not-applicable due to clear conditions
Month 6: next winter approaches, mark archive valuable for re-emerging risk
cases.human_judgment: Seasonal alpine danger that disappears in summer but absolutely returns in winter. Mark must persist year-round even when summer reports say not-applicable. Killing in summer means winter cohort loses 5 months of aggregated knowledge.

cases.title: Old Ghost Road 5-day Ghost Lake Hut mountain bike collision warning

scenario.location_desc: Old Ghost Road 80km 4-5 day bike or hike, blind corner descent before Ghost Lake Hut, multiple near-collisions between uphill hikers and downhill bikers reported by hut group on day 3
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Real injury risk at blind-corner shared-use trail
scenario.signal: no signal entire trail, syncs at Lyell or Seddonville
scenario.season_pattern: year round but bike volume peaks summer
scenario.human_factors: bikers and hikers both motivated to warn, cross-mode mark

events_timeline: Month 1: hiker hut group posts after near-miss, photos of blind corner
Month 2: 6 bikers and 4 hikers confirm same corner, 25 likes
Month 3: trail trust adds physical warning signage
Month 5: post-signage users confirm signs help but bikers still fast
Month 8: 40 likes, ongoing advisory rather than fixed
Month 12: stable advisory, integrates into pre-trip briefing materials
cases.human_judgment: Multi-modal trail with inherent geometric hazard not fully solvable by signage. Mark should remain alive as ongoing advisory rather than resolved, because the underlying blind-corner physics doesn't change. Both biker and hiker likes show cross-mode validation.

cases.title: Hump Ridge Track Stag Point sandflies extreme on day 2 of 3

scenario.location_desc: Hump Ridge Track 3-day Tuatapere Fiordland, Stag Point lookout has extreme sandfly density during westerly humid days, found on day 2 by group running out of repellent
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Sandfly density real and impactful, worst in NZ tied with West Coast
scenario.signal: limited at lookout, sync at Tuatapere
scenario.season_pattern: Nov-Mar peak, year round otherwise present
scenario.human_factors: well-known but always shocks first-timers

events_timeline: Month 1: tourist group posts mark, 50 sandfly bites count, very vivid description
Month 2: locals comment well-known thing, suggest mark redundant with general knowledge
Month 3: 12 international visitors thank for warning, 30 likes
Month 5: track concession adds repellent vending machine at hut
Month 7: 45 likes, mark stable as international-visitor advisory
Month 8: track marketing references mark as community resource
cases.human_judgment: Locals say redundant but international visitors have no Aotearoa sandfly priors. Mark serves the audience that needs it. Local-knowledge dismissal is exactly the bias the system must filter out. Volume of likes from international users is the real signal.

cases.title: Kepler Track Iris Burn Hut helicopter resupply noise pattern day 3

scenario.location_desc: Kepler Track 4-day Te Anau, Iris Burn Hut campsite gets helicopter resupply Tuesday mornings 7am, mark warns wilderness-experience seekers, posted by user who chose Tue night by mistake
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Wilderness experience expectation management
scenario.signal: limited, sync at Te Anau
scenario.season_pattern: Great Walk season helicopter scheduled, off-season unpredictable
scenario.human_factors: user posts so others can choose Wed or Mon nights instead

events_timeline: Month 1: original poster makes mark with 7am helicopter video
Month 2: 8 confirmations of Tuesday pattern, 35 likes
Month 3: DOC concession confirms scheduled resupply, suggests booking pattern
Month 4: smart users start booking Wed-Sun avoiding Tue, mark drives behavior
Month 5: 50 likes, mark stable as practical scheduling advisory
Month 6: confirmed-useful by tourism boards
cases.human_judgment: Mark drives actual booking behavior change. Not danger, not facility, but high practical value. System should value behavior-impact marks even when they sound trivial. Pattern-based marks (every Tuesday) are uniquely user-discoverable, DOC won't post these.

cases.title: Abel Tasman inland track 3-day vs coast disagreement post-trip

scenario.location_desc: Abel Tasman Inland Track 3-day separate from coast track, mark says better wilderness than coast, but user came back to it after coastal track on day 4 of combined trip and disagreed
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Subjective comparison, opinion shifts after seeing both
scenario.signal: limited inland, full at Marahau or Totaranui
scenario.season_pattern: year round inland track
scenario.human_factors: opinion changed after experiencing both routes back-to-back

events_timeline: Month 1: original poster marks inland better, 15 likes
Month 4: combined-trip user reports inland not better after seeing coast, suggests downgrade
Month 6: 5 more combined-trip users add nuance, both have value
Month 9: mark text edited by community to comparative not absolute
Month 11: 25 likes, stable nuanced version
Month 14: mark serves as decision aid rather than absolute claim
cases.human_judgment: Mark improved through community editing from absolute to comparative claim. This is the system working: opinion shifts after broader context naturally refine the mark. Should NOT kill, the evolution itself is the value. Combined-trip users have higher epistemic standing than single-route.

cases.title: Milford Track Mintaro Hut bunk allocation on rainy day 2 of 4

scenario.location_desc: Milford Track 4-day Great Walk, Mintaro Hut on heavy rain day 2 the drying room overcrowded and bunks 1-3 closest to the door soaked, posted by user who got soaked
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Bunk choice strategy specific to weather, granular and useful
scenario.signal: limited, syncs at Milford Sound or Te Anau
scenario.season_pattern: Great Walk season high volume Oct-Apr
scenario.human_factors: Milford peak volume means rapid validation

events_timeline: Month 1: rainy-day user posts with photo of soaked bunk 2
Month 2: 12 confirmations, 40 likes within month
Month 3: DOC concession comments noted, working on door seal
Month 4: door seal fixed, post-fix user reports bunks dry, suggests resolved
Month 6: 55 likes, mark transitioned to historical advisory
Month 7: stable, used by next-season trip planners
cases.human_judgment: Mark drove physical hut improvement (door seal). After resolved, retain as evidence of community-to-DOC feedback loop. Future similar issues benefit when users see their reports lead to actual fixes. Killing the mark erases that institutional memory.

cases.title: Cape Brett Track day-3 cumulative knee pain mark questionable validity

scenario.location_desc: Cape Brett Track 16km return 2-3 days, mark warns of treacherous knee-killing descent, posted by user on day 3 with cumulative 30km of fatigue, suspected fatigue-bias
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Real terrain difficulty but exaggerated by fatigue context
scenario.signal: patchy on cape, sync at Russell or Rawhiti
scenario.season_pattern: year round but wet winter increases mud difficulty
scenario.human_factors: fatigue-bias real consideration, fresh hikers report easier

events_timeline: Month 1: cumulative-fatigue user posts danger mark, intense tone
Month 2: fresh dayhikers report descent moderate not treacherous, 5 reports
Month 4: 10 multi-day users confirm cumulative-fatigue version, 18 likes
Month 6: physiotherapist comments knee strain plausible after 30km cumulative
Month 8: mark text edited to advisory contingent on cumulative load
Month 10: stable nuanced version, distinguishes day-3 vs day-1 experience
cases.human_judgment: Mark validity depends on whether user is on day 1 or day 3. System needs to capture context-dependent truth, not flatten to alive-or-dead. Reports from fresh dayhikers shouldn't kill mark useful to multi-day users; they're describing different experiences of the same terrain.

cases.title: Pouakai Circuit Mt Taranaki tarn reflection mark cloudy on day 2 of 3

scenario.location_desc: Pouakai Circuit 2-3 day Mt Taranaki, the iconic Pouakai Tarns reflection of Taranaki posted as world-class scenic, day-2 user found cloud-covered mountain and questioned
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Real iconic scenery when conditions allow, weather dependent
scenario.signal: patchy on circuit, syncs at New Plymouth
scenario.season_pattern: year round but Taranaki weather notoriously fickle
scenario.human_factors: frustrated cloud-day users vs blue-sky users diverge sharply

events_timeline: Month 1: original blue-sky photographer marks the scenic with hero photo
Month 2: cloudy-day user reports mountain not visible, suggests downgrade
Month 3: 8 blue-sky users confirm iconic, 30 likes
Month 5: weather forecaster comments mountain visible 40 percent of summer days
Month 7: 50 likes 6 reports, mark stable as canonical with weather caveat
Month 11: long-term stable, mark text references weather statistics
cases.human_judgment: Cloud-day reports are real experience but not falsification of underlying scenery. Mark for iconic-when-clear must survive cloudy votes; otherwise every weather-dependent NZ peak loses its mark. Statistical caveat (40 percent visibility) is good evolution, killing is wrong.

cases.title: Tongariro Northern Circuit Oturere Hut bunkroom snoring symphony day 3

scenario.location_desc: Tongariro Northern Circuit 3-4 day, Oturere Hut large bunkroom severe snoring from group of 8, day-3 sleep-deprived user marks as advisory to bring earplugs
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Sleep-quality practical advisory, well-meaning
scenario.signal: limited, sync at Whakapapa
scenario.season_pattern: Great Walk season high volume
scenario.human_factors: subjective but consistent across many trips

events_timeline: Month 1: sleep-deprived user posts earplugs advisory
Month 2: 6 confirmations of similar experiences, 22 likes
Month 3: DOC posts joke comment that all huts have this problem
Month 4: 30 likes, no reports, light-hearted but useful
Month 5: stable as bring-earplugs reminder for hut sleepers
cases.human_judgment: Low-stakes but high-value-for-sleep mark. System should not bias toward only Serious Safety marks. Volume of grateful likes shows genuine utility. Earplug recommendation is the kind of practical wisdom DOC won't post but every hut user wants.

cases.title: Cascade Saddle Glenorchy track plummet warning team consensus on day 4

scenario.location_desc: Cascade Saddle from Dart Hut side 5-day, the Pylon descent infamous for fatal slips in wet conditions, posted by team of 4 who debated 30 minutes whether to descend on day 4 wet morning
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Genuine fatal-fall terrain, multiple deaths historically
scenario.signal: no signal at saddle, sync at Glenorchy
scenario.season_pattern: Dec-Mar season, otherwise officially closed
scenario.human_factors: team consensus mark with high deliberation, high credibility

events_timeline: Month 1: 4-person team posts collective danger mark with deliberation notes
Month 3: NZAC veteran adds incident history, 15 likes
Month 6: DOC alpine alerts cite the user mark for current conditions
Month 12: ongoing advisory, periodic confirmations every season
Month 18: 28 likes, mark canonical for this descent
Month 21: stable, referenced in NZAC handbook updates
cases.human_judgment: Team-consensus mark with documented deliberation is the highest-quality user mark. Multi-person agreement after debate carries more signal than 10 solo posts. System should reward provenance, not just count likes. Cascade Saddle has killed people; this mark is forever.

cases.title: Wangapeka Track Stone Hut firewood absent on cold day 4 of 5

scenario.location_desc: Wangapeka Track 4-5 day Kahurangi, Stone Hut firewood pile empty on day 4 of trip, group of 3 cold-soaked, suspected previous group took everything
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Cold-night risk, firewood etiquette problem
scenario.signal: no signal, sync at Tapawera or Karamea
scenario.season_pattern: matters cold months Apr-Oct
scenario.human_factors: fellow-tramper antagonism, advisory tone

events_timeline: Month 1: cold group posts firewood-empty mark, polite but pointed
Month 2: 4 winter trampers confirm pattern of empty pile, 14 likes
Month 3: DOC volunteer comments hut warden checks monthly, leaves logs
Month 5: post-restock users confirm logs there, suggests cyclical not chronic
Month 7: stable, mark functions as please-leave-some advisory
Month 8: integrated into hut culture reminder
cases.human_judgment: Mark addresses tramper-vs-tramper etiquette not infrastructure. Resolution by DOC restocking misses the point; the pattern is human behavior. Should remain as ongoing community reminder. Future winter cohorts benefit from awareness even after current restock.

cases.title: Stewart Island Northwest Circuit mud reality day 6 of 9

scenario.location_desc: Stewart Island Rakiura Northwest Circuit 9-11 day, day 6 user marks knee-deep mud through Mason Bay section, common knowledge but first-timers underestimate
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Real mud reality, gear-failure risk wet feet for days
scenario.signal: no signal entire circuit, sync at Oban after exit
scenario.season_pattern: year round mud, slightly drier Feb
scenario.human_factors: experienced trampers know but international visitors shocked

events_timeline: Month 1: international visitor posts mud-shock mark from Oban ferry wifi
Month 4: 3 more international visitors confirm, locals comment well-known
Month 8: 12 likes mostly international, 2 dismissive local reports
Month 14: tourism brochure starts citing the user mark
Month 17: 18 likes, established as international-visitor advisory
Month 19: stable, helpful for first-timer expectation setting
